name: Tiller & Persinger 2002: 'Thomas' FM pattern, 3-ms points, right (5 min)
origin: Tiller & Persinger 2002 (Laurentian University); 'Thomas' pattern after Alex W. Thomas (US 6,234,953)
summary: The 849-point 'Thomas' frequency-modulated table of US 6,234,953, played at 3 ms per point as the lab later described (a 2.55-s decelerating burst, repeated), over the right parietotemporal region at 1 uT for 5 min. Tiller & Persinger 2002 (12 people) reported that 40% of all left-sided presences came during this one 5-min configuration and that the time-reversed pattern was less effective.
notes: Tiller & Persinger applied eight 1-uT configurations for 5 min each 'primarily over the right parietotemporal region', in an order the subjects did not know, and logged button presses as left, right or front-back presences. Only this pattern and its time-reversed copy (persinger-tiller-2002-thomas-reversed) are identified; the other six ('more or less complex') were never published, so this file holds the effective block alone. The table is Table 1 of US 6,234,953 (Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger), 849 points, which the lab replayed at 3 ms per point (Buckner 2015; Murugan 2013); that Tiller used this very file is the lab's later description, not stated in the 2002 abstract. A 3-ms pause after each pass (the 3-ms pixel plus 3-ms interstimulus optimum Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999 found in rats) gives Buckner's 2.55-s cycle; the lab's rat analgesia version was 837 values of 1 ms once every 4 s (Dixon & Persinger 2001). Within it 18 pulses slow from about 12 to 5 per second (the lab's '25 to 6 Hz' labels do not follow from the table). Sites T8 and TP8 are an inference; the left channels stay silent. A 5-s fade is added at start and end. The lab otherwise held that subjective effects need 20-40 min per pattern (see persinger-cook-2001-fm-right); this study used 5 min. For a blinded test, have someone else pick this file, the reversed file or a sham, and note the time and side of anything you feel. n = 12, within-subject, one lab; the side of a presence is a subjective report and has never been tested independently. Granqvist et al. ran 15 min of the Thomas pattern over the right hemisphere, then 15 min of bilateral burst-firing, double-blind with 89 people, and found no field effect; Persinger blamed uncalibrated Windows timing and the short exposure. Independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop at once on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Blindfolded or with opaque goggles in a quiet, dark room; press a button, speak, or tell a helper the moment anything is felt and on which side (left, right, front or back).
schedule: One 5-min block in the original, one of eight 5-min configurations given to each subject in an order they did not know. At most once a week.
source: Tiller & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:26 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11883572/ ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (849 points at 3 ms, 2.55-s cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Murugan 2013, thesis, Laurentian University, pp. 44-45 (248-point burst-x, 849-point Thomas pulse, 3-ms points) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/39c9c1ad-70ba-458d-a819-d24c20da217a ; Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999, Percept Mot Skills 89:486 (3-ms pixel and interstimulus optimum in rats) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10597585/ ; Dixon & Persinger 2001, Int J Neurosci 108:87 (837 values at 1 ms, once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11328704/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Persinger & Koren 2005, A response to Granqvist et al., Neurosci Lett 380:346 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15862915/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
